result: Implement ModSettings.cs as the sole typed contract: ModSettingDefinition {Id,ModName,SettingType:startup|runtime,ValueType:bool|int|double|string|enum|color,Default,Minimum,Maximum,AllowedValues,Required}; ModSettingValue as a discriminated primitive/color union; ModSettingsCompatibility {FactorioVersion,Expansion,SaveName,SaveSha256,EnabledMods[{Name,Version,Sha256}],CatalogFingerprint}; ModSettingsArtifact {SchemaVersion,GeneratedAtUtc,Compatibility,Values}; ModSettingsDocument {Artifact,Definitions}. Discover definitions from the selected version's base/expansion data and enabled mod archives/files by parsing supported settings.lua declarations and reject malformed/unsupported declarations with diagnostics. Persist only the validated manager artifact at config/mod-settings.json using temp-file-plus-atomic-replace and retain the prior artifact for rollback; never accept arbitrary keys, unknown settings, invalid types, out-of-range numbers, disallowed enum values, or values for disabled mods. Add GET /api/mod-settings/catalog and GET /api/mod-settings, plus PUT /api/mod-settings accepting {artifact,confirmStopped}; require owner/admin authorization, CSRF, confirmStopped=true, and supervisor.IsRunning=false, returning 409 while running. Compute compatibility from active version, expansion, enabled ModEntry metadata, selected save basename and SHA-256; GET must report stale/mismatched compatibility and PUT must reject stale artifacts unless the request includes a freshly matching compatibility snapshot. ServerSupervisor must load/validate the artifact before startup, materialize the Factorio-supported mod-settings input without exposing secrets, and fail closed on invalid/stale startup settings; runtime changes remain persisted and applied only through the stopped-server workflow, with no live RCON mutation. App.tsx should add a typed catalog editor grouped by setting type/mod, show defaults/constraints and compatibility warnings, disable edits while running, require an explicit stopped confirmation, and preserve server-error responses. Add focused persistence/validation tests for discovery, all primitive types and constraints, unknown/disabled-mod rejection, atomic rollback, compatibility drift, stopped-server enforcement, and startup fail-closed behavior; preserve MapControlCatalog behavior and existing save-create partition tests.

evidence.outcome: Existing records use immutable public DTOs; ServerSettings owns active version, expansion, and active save, while ModEntry carries enabled-mod version, source, archive filename, and SHA-256 metadata.
Authenticated API groups already apply CSRF filters; settings and mod mutations enforce stopped-server checks and provide the route boundary for new typed endpoints.

Startup writes server-settings.json and mod-list.json from persisted state, and save creation separately passes map-gen-settings and map-settings; mod-settings loading belongs in the same pre-start validation path.

ModService already validates archives/info.json, dependency graphs, Factorio compatibility, transactional recovery, and enabled-mod state; discovery should reuse its canonical installed ModEntry set and archive paths.
Existing version/expansion/enabled-mod catalog contract is a prerequisite and must remain unchanged; its content fingerprint is suitable compatibility metadata.
Config is the durable host-mounted location for manager-generated artifacts; Mods, Versions, and Saves provide the discovery inputs.
SQLite app_state supports additive metadata, but the validated settings artifact should remain an atomic file so deployment and rollback are inspectable.
Tests establish isolated DataRoot fixtures, JSON persistence conventions, stopped-state validation, map catalog behavior, and save-create serializer partition coverage.
Mod mutations use crash-recoverable journals and quarantine malformed state; mod-settings writes need equivalent atomic recovery semantics.
Durable config/mod/save data is host-mounted, and changes affecting a running server are intentionally stopped-server gated.

next_slice.summary: Implement the typed ModSettings contract, discovery/validation service, atomic artifact persistence, compatibility snapshot, API routes, and stopped/startup enforcement; then add App.tsx editor and focused persistence/API tests. First verify the installed Factorio executable's accepted --mod-settings input format before finalizing materialization; keep manager JSON separate if Factorio requires a binary/generated format.
